candidate: One physical wave32 serially executes the current dual-split kernel's four virtual-wave block-index sequences, preserving each wave reduction and the ordered four-part final sum while eliminating physical cross-wave exchange.
distinction_from_prior_work: The historical all-body block64 candidate changed K ownership and reduction order, changed generated IDs, and regressed full-model throughput. This candidate targeted only dual-split and emulated the exact 128-thread arithmetic order.

correctness.contract: Candidate BF16 output bytes equal the current 128-thread body for ordinary and all-output-repeated weight fixtures.

micro_protocol.timing: HIP events; median of six per-call leg means

decision: Reject at the predeclared cache-cycled leaf gate and remove all candidate code/tests. Serial execution of the four exact virtual waves costs 55.14% more than the current four-wave body, so cross-wave exchange is not removable under the existing 16-output-per-thread T16 mapping. No profiler or full-model run is warranted.
